channel.title: Global Arbitration Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Global Arbitration Review (globalarbitrationreview.com)

item.title: Ecuador averts ICSID claim with release of pipeline guarantees
item.description: A Cayman subsidiary of Argentina’s Pampa Energía has dropped an ICSID claim against Ecuador after securing the release of guarantees worth US$100 million relating to the handover of an oil pipeline concession.

item.title: Partasides on the deterrent effect of contempt
item.description: In a speech in Houston, Constantine Partasides KC of Three Crowns considered “counter-insurgency techniques” to address party and counsel misconduct in arbitration and whether it is time to recognise “the arbitral equivalent of... contempt of court.”

item.title: Eni spars with partner over Sicilian gas field
item.description: A London and Tel Aviv-listed energy company says it is pursuing claims worth €265 million against its joint venture partner Eni in an arbitration over a gas field off the coast of Sicily.

item.title: Honduras to rejoin ICSID after Trump ally takes office
item.description: Honduras’ new conservative president Nasry Asfura has given notice of the country’s intent to rejoin the ICSID Convention – on the same day he was sworn in after narrowly winning elections with the vocal support of US President Donald Trump.

item.title: Ecuador asks Constitutional Court to approve BIT with UAE
item.description: Ecuador has asked its Constitutional Court to rule that a new bilateral investment treaty with the United Arab Emirates can be ratified without prior approval by the National Assembly, a move that puts investor-state arbitration back under constitutional scrutiny. Hernán Pérez Loose and Julia Rovello of Coronel y Pérez report.

item.title: Pérez-Llorca hires in Colombia
item.description: Spanish firm Pérez-Llorca has recruited Felipe Suescún de Roa as partner in Bogotá, while promoting Daragh Brehony to counsel in Madrid.

item.title: New practice head at Houthoff
item.description: Thomas Stouten has been appointed the new head of international arbitration at Houthoff, taking over from Dirk Knottenbelt.

item.title: Mourre shares his take on abuse of process
item.description: In a speech at King's College London before the New Year, Alexis Mourre considered abuse of process in international arbitration with reference to "diametrically opposed conclusions" on the matter from Emmanuel Gaillard and Jan Paulsson.

item.title: Libya revives challenge to Turkish contractor’s award
item.description: The French courts have enforced a final award in a treaty claim against Libya relating to three construction projects, while reviving the state’s challenge to a jurisdictional award in the same case.

item.title: US gymnast wins challenge to CAS award as Gharavi cleared of conflict
item.description: A Swiss court has granted a request by US gymnast Jordan Chiles to reopen a high-profile Court of Arbitration for Sport award that effectively stripped her of an Olympic bronze medal – while dismissing her claims that the presiding arbitrator Hamid Gharavi had a conflict of interests.
